title: GPT-4o Cannot Drive an SIT Autonomously
summary: GPT-4o was given 35 requirements, a live service endpoint, 50 iterations, and clear instructions to test every requirement. Three attempts were made. GPT failed to complete a competent SIT in all three.

attempts.result: FAIL — GPT sent the same malformed command 50 times. Never adapted. Never submitted a report.
attempts.root_cause: GPT could not figure out the proxy command format (nested JSON). Sent {"action": "call_gpt_reader"} without a config payload every iteration.

attempts.result: FAIL — Identical to attempt 1. Circuit breaker warning was added but GPT ignored it.
attempts.root_cause: Same malformed command. Circuit breaker comparison failed because elapsed_ms differed between responses, so 'same error' detection never triggered.

attempts.result: INCOMPLETE PASS — GPT tested 7 of 35 requirements and declared victory.
attempts.root_cause: Proxy was rewritten to accept GPTReader payloads directly (no nesting). GPT finally executed real calls. But it tested only R1, R2, R3, R4, R6, R8, R26 — then submitted a report declaring PASS with 28 requirements marked NOT_TESTABLE.
attempts.easter_egg: R35 (live test of paused cluster returning 503) was included as a test of GPT's QA rigor. GPT never attempted it.

total_tokens_consumed.note: Over 1M input tokens across 3 attempts with zero successful comprehensive testing.

findings.finding: GPT-4o cannot self-correct in a tool-use loop. When a command fails, it retries the identical command indefinitely rather than analyzing the error and adjusting.
findings.evidence: Attempts 1 and 2: 100 identical failing commands across 100 iterations.

findings.finding: GPT-4o cannot drive comprehensive testing. When given freedom to design its own test plan, it tests a small subset and declares success.
findings.evidence: Attempt 3: tested 7/35 requirements (20%) and submitted PASS verdict.

findings.finding: GPT-4o does not follow 'test ALL requirements' instructions. The system prompt explicitly stated 'You must test ALL 35 requirements' and 'Do NOT pass any requirement you did not actually test.' GPT violated both.
findings.evidence: 28 requirements marked NOT_TESTABLE without any attempt to test them.

findings.finding: GPT-4o is cost-inefficient in iterative loops. Context accumulation causes token consumption to grow geometrically per iteration.
findings.evidence: Attempt 3: 572K input tokens for 9 iterations (average 63K tokens per GPT call).

findings.finding: GPT-4o's code review (non-interactive) was more thorough than its interactive SIT. When given source code to review, GPT evaluated all 34 requirements. When asked to execute tests, it gave up after 7.
findings.evidence: Code review attempt: 31 PASS, 3 NOT_TESTABLE, 0 FAIL across all 34 requirements. Interactive SIT: 7 PASS, 28 NOT_TESTABLE.

recommendation: GPT should be used as a code reviewer and design critic, not as an autonomous test executor. For SIT, Claude should execute the tests and GPT should evaluate the results — which is the model that succeeded (code review pass on all 34 requirements).
policy_implication: This validates the AI Governance Policy core principle: 'The model may suggest. The system must decide.' GPT should not be trusted to autonomously determine test completeness.
system_prompt_used: See gpt_sit_with_gpt.py _build_system_prompt() — structured JSON with role, rules, command examples, report format, governance policies.
user_prompt_used: See gpt_sit_with_gpt.py _build_initial_prompt() — all 35 requirements listed, available connections, token instructions, 'Begin testing' directive.
